Outline mode is the product, and it is currently invisible: a per-file toggle reachable only
from editing modes, whose only feedback is a 1.5s toast, and every new file starts stock
unless toggled by hand. This makes the mode an explicit, persistent, visible state.

`docs/research/24-outline-mode-surfaces.md` records the surface research and the measurements
this rests on; `openspec/changes/per-tab-outline-mode/` carries the proposal, design and tasks.

## What changes

**BREAKING — the mode becomes a per-tab state with a global default.** A new setting, "open new
tabs in outline mode", on by default, governs every note a tab newly opens. The per-file
`outlinePaths` store retires with no migration: `normalizePluginData`'s allow-list drops the key
on the first save. An upgrading install's next file open is outlined, which is deliberate.

- **The toggle acts on the active tab only**, and a tab's manual state is ephemeral — it dies
  with the tab's editor state, exactly as a pane's zoom scope already does. Two tabs on one file
  can differ.
- **Changing the setting touches future opens only**, like the core "default view mode for new
  tabs" setting it mirrors.
- **The toggle works from any view mode** — `checkCallback` over the active `MarkdownView`
  rather than `editorCheckCallback`, so the palette offers it in reading view too. Toggling ON
  from reading view switches the pane to its own last editing mode via the public `View.setState`
  route, over an off default and a manual off alike; OFF from reading view is a no-op.
- **A visible indication:** a status bar item (desktop) and a ribbon icon (both platforms), each
  stating the ACTIVE tab's state and toggling that tab on click. The toast stays — on mobile it
  is the only immediate feedback.

## The measurement that moved the design

The change's first task probed a real Obsidian rather than reasoning from the API, and answered
more than it asked. The reading-view state round-trips its own `source` flag, so the entry needs
no default. No public event fires on an in-leaf mode switch. And **Obsidian keeps one
`EditorView` per leaf and rebuilds its `EditorState` only on a file switch** — so a `StateField`
resets on a new tab and on a note switch, and NOT on a reading round-trip.

Design D4 had assumed all three rebuild the editor, and the specs said a reading round-trip
resets the tab. Both are corrected to the measured boundary: a manual state now survives a
reading round-trip, which is also the better behaviour — flipping to reading view to check
something is not a request to undo a manual off — and forcing a reset would need a signal
Obsidian does not give.

## How it is built

The per-tab state is a boolean `StateField` (`src/plugin/outline-state.ts`, obsidian-free like
`zoom-state.ts`), initialized from the setting at editor-state construction and flipped by one
effect dispatched through the existing view registry. The gating seam moves with it — grammar,
decorations, transaction filter, backlinks footer and the zoom gates read the field through one
shared helper instead of `isOutline(path)`, so `ModeSource` retires and `zoomScope` loses its
mode argument. That is the change's largest code movement and it pays for itself: a mode toggle
becomes a real CM6 transaction, so every consumer recomputes because the field moved, and the
cursor-nudge sweep, the per-leaf `forceRedraw` pass and `OutlineModeRegistry`'s ordered write
queue all retire.

Three things turned out to work only *because* reaching outline mode used to mean toggling into
it, which dispatched a cursor nudge from outside CM6. The full sweep found all three, and each
is fixed at its own layer: `MarginCompensation`'s layout-dependent measurements now take a
deferred pass (a note that opens already decorated produces no `docViewUpdate`); the
block-selection focus policy now also runs when the mode field moves (a mode change is an exit
and is not a selection change); and `outline-zoom`'s exit trigger 3 narrows to the view whose
mode turned off, which is what its own per-view scope model always implied.

## Verification

`e2e/specs/10-outline-mode.e2e.ts` is rewritten for the per-tab lifecycle and
`11-outline-mode-surfaces.e2e.ts` is new, both green under desktop and mobile emulation. The
mobile pass earned its keep twice: `addStatusBarItem` still returns a live element under
`emulateMobile()` despite its desktop-only documentation, so it is gated on `Platform.isMobile`.

Every new claim was confirmed to fail with its mechanism disabled — including the fresh-install
case, whose first version passed against any default because the harness had written the value
it was reading.

Full suite: `npm test` 7022 passing, `npm run lint` clean, `npm run test:e2e` 38 specs / 607
passing / 0 failing.

**Yes, the review is partly outdated.** Copilot ran against commit 1 of 6, when the branch held only planning artifacts:

- **Comment 2 (missing implementation) — outdated.** The PR now has 6 commits / 62 changed files, including `src/plugin/outline-state.ts`, the gating-seam move across every extension, `tests/outline-state.test.ts`, and both e2e specs. Replied on the thread explaining; no change needed.

The answer the measurement gives is neither: a pane keeps its editor across a view-mode switch, so a reading-view tab still *has* a state and the indicators report that one. It now round-trips through a second tab to force a re-read, and the negative control fires.

Consequences worth naming:

- **The per-tab state is ephemeral by mechanism.** It lives in the editor view (the same shape
  `outline-zoom` gives its scope: per view, never persisted), so it dies not only when the tab
  closes but also when the tab switches notes or round-trips through reading view — the editor
  is rebuilt in those cases, and the fresh one initializes from the default. "Until it's
  closed" is only approximately achievable; strictly tab-scoped persistence needs leaf-keyed
  state outside the editor and was rejected.
- **No per-file memory at all.** A note reopened later starts from the default every time; a
  remembered opt-out would be an explicit-off list with its own rename/delete hygiene — the
  next number in this series if real use demands it.
- **Changing the setting touches future opens only**, mirroring the built-in "default view
  mode for new tabs" setting it was modeled on; already-open tabs are not retoggled.
- **Two tabs on one file can differ**, exactly as two panes already hold different zoom
  scopes.
- **Upgrade flips behavior.** An existing install's next file open after the update outlines
  every newly opened note (the default is on; Obsidian updates do not rewrite settings a user
=== D7 design 130-145
between them cover every transition that can change the answer.

An in-leaf mode switch fires no public event (measured), and needs none: the same measurement
says the field does not change across one, so the mode the indicators state is still the mode
the tab is in. The staleness this decision originally hedged against cannot arise — a stale
label would require a mode change with no event, and a mode change is either a dispatch through
the toggle path or a fresh `EditorState`, and both are covered.

`addStatusBarItem()` is registered unconditionally (documented as unavailable on mobile,
asserted by the mobile e2e; a `Platform.isMobile` gate is the one-line fallback). The ribbon
icon is `list-tree` — the menu entry's icon — with a class-reflecting on-state; both click into
the same toggle path as the command. Wording and on-state treatment are one visual pass in the
tasks, recorded in docs/research/24, the way the decoration experiments settled theirs.

### D8. The settings toggle sets the default, and nothing else

Declarative `getSettingDefinitions()` toggle plus the pre-1.13 `display()` fallback, kept in
sync; the setter persists and does NOT sweep open tabs — the spec states "changing it SHALL
NOT retoggle already-open tabs", and per D4 there is nothing to sweep: future constructions
pick the new value up at `init`. Discoverable wording states the semantics ("new tabs only")
and names the other surfaces.

fix(outline-mode): address the second review round

Two real defects, both found by review rather than by a test.

`outlineStateExtension` bound the default through a module-level handle, so the
binding was shared rather than the extension's: a second call retargeted every
editor built from the first one. The plugin loads once so nothing in the app saw
it, but the unit suite is already a second caller, and a shared mutable that is
only correct because there happens to be one caller is a trap for the next. It
now uses `outlineModeField.init(() => source.outlineByDefault)`, which keeps the
live read and binds it to the extension; a new test covers two sources side by
side and fails against the old shape.

`scheduleRemeasure` treated every zero-width measurement as a one-frame layout
delay. A HIDDEN view measures zero indefinitely — an inactive tab and the editor
retained behind reading view are both display:none — so it re-armed a frame
callback per hidden outlined editor, forever. It now asks whether the VIEW has a
box: if not, a self-disconnecting ResizeObserver waits for one instead of the
frame clock.

Accessibility: the status bar item was focusable with `role="button"` and
handled only clicks, so Enter and Space did nothing; it now takes both, with
`preventDefault` for Space, the way `backlinks-footer.ts`'s disclosures do. And
both indicators carry `aria-pressed` — the ribbon's whole state signal was a
colour, which a screen reader cannot see and its unchanging label does not say —
removed rather than set when no markdown tab is active, since neither value is
true of a control stating no mode.

Contract: the editor context menu deliberately acts on the editor it was opened
in, which need not be the active tab, while the requirement said every surface
acts on the active tab. The requirement now states the exception and why the
right-click is what names the editor meant, with a scenario for it. The
settings description no longer says "new tabs only", which hid that an existing
tab switching notes also picks up the new default.

Docs: docs/research/24's consequences still described a reading round-trip as a
reset, contradicting the measurement later in the same note; design D7 still
said the status item registers unconditionally, which the `Platform.isMobile`
gate superseded. Both corrected. The mobile ribbon helper now checks for a box
rather than branching on platform, so a real click is used wherever one is
possible — measured: `leftSplit.expand()` does open the mobile drawer, and the
drawer's ribbon column stays display:none either way, because the emulator is
the desktop shell in a phone viewport. What no run here can cover, that a real
mobile user can see and press it, is recorded as a manual check.

tasks.md gains the two landing steps its own Migration Plan names — archive and
`npm version minor` — left unchecked, since the version bump is what makes CI
cut a release and belongs immediately before the merge.

All eight threads replied to and resolved; pushed as `0b69a09`.

**On your question — you're right, and the answer is that I overran the practice.** Task 5.5 required one full local sweep before the checkpoint, so that one was in scope. The two after it were not: CI's per-group matrix already covers a pushed checkpoint, and narrow runs on the specs I touched were the correct local check. I also used the window-popping variant instead of `test:e2e:docker`, so I took over your screen for ~11 minutes twice for something CI does better. Won't repeat it.

**Two real defects in this round, both found by review rather than by a test:**

- **`outline-state.ts` bound the default through a module-level handle** — shared, not per-extension, so a second call retargeted editors built from the first. The plugin loads once so the app never saw it, but the unit suite is already a second caller. Now `outlineModeField.init(...)`; the new test fails against the old shape.
- **`scheduleRemeasure` re-armed forever on hidden views.** An inactive tab and the editor behind reading view are both `display:none`, so "zero width" wasn't a one-frame delay — it re-armed a frame callback per hidden editor indefinitely. It now checks whether the *view* has a box and hands off to a self-disconnecting `ResizeObserver`.

Also fixed: keyboard activation on the status item, `aria-pressed` on both indicators (the ribbon's only state signal was colour), the context-menu contract mismatch — the implementation was right and the requirement was wrong, so the requirement now states the exception — the misleading "new tabs only" setting text, and two stale doc passages.

**One thing I could not do as asked.** Copilot wanted the mobile ribbon test to exercise the user-visible control or fail. I measured first: `leftSplit.expand()` *does* open the mobile drawer, but the drawer's ribbon column stays `display:none` regardless, because the emulator is the desktop shell in a phone viewport. Failing there would assert an emulator defect, so the helper now checks for a clickable box rather than branching on platform — real click wherever possible, upgrading itself if a build ever renders the row — and the genuinely uncovered part (a real mobile user seeing and pressing it) is recorded as a manual check.

**Unresolved, for you:** the full local sweep showed 4 failures (`56-list-grid`, `62-outline-edit-enforcement`, `63-selection-visual-treatment`, `80-outline-zoom`) that **all pass when run narrowly**. The previous full sweep was 607/0 before the `ResizeObserver` and `init()` changes, so I can't yet tell contention from a real cross-spec effect of the observer — and per your own practice CI's matrix is the arbiter. It's running on the push now; if it reports them, I'll fix them.

Still held for your go: `openspec archive per-tab-outline-mode` and `npm version minor` (tasks 6.3/6.4). The bump triggers the release, so I'm not running it unasked.

Two adjustments from a manual pass.

The ribbon icon can be hidden from Obsidian's own right-click menu; a plugin's
status bar item cannot, so "I don't want this one" had no answer. A
`statusBarMode` setting now shapes it: an icon, the state in words, or nothing.

ribbon's colour accent — a tinted chip competes for attention with everything
else in that bar, while `align-left`'s flat prose lines against `list-tree`'s
branching ones survive being small and monochrome.

the document now visibly changes under a state both indicators already report,
so a toast is a third report of the same fact delivered by interruption.

`setOutlineMode` and the new `waitForOutlineMode` settle on the STATE, which a
notice never asserted — it only ever said the command had run. Every
toggle-then-wait-for-notice pair across eleven specs moves to it. The
reading-view entry tests keep their explicit `toggleOutlineMode` and wait on the

content.text:
Both adjustments are in, pushed as `8d2993a`.

**Status bar chip — `none | text | icon`, default `icon`.** The reasoning you gave (ribbon is user-hideable, status bar isn't) is now the setting's stated justification. `none` renders nothing and drops out of the keyboard tab order — `addStatusBarItem` has no counterpart, so an empty hidden element *is* the off state.

**On the off-state icon:** you were right that a second glyph is needed. I went with `list-tree` (on) / `align-left` (off) rather than any accent — flat prose lines against branching ones, which is a contrast that survives being small and monochrome, and it keeps the noise out of the bar as you asked. The ribbon keeps its colour accent, since there it's the only signal available. Easy to swap if `align-left` doesn't read right to you in situ.

**Toast dropped.** Also removed from the spec, which had required it ("SHALL remain on every toggle from every surface") — that clause existed for a world where nothing else reported the mode.

One thing worth flagging: **the harness lost its settle signal, and the replacement is stronger.** Eleven specs were waiting on `waitForNotice('Outline mode …')` after a toggle; they now wait on the actual state via `setOutlineMode`/`waitForOutlineMode`. A notice only ever proved the command had run — the state is what the tests actually meant. ---
/**
 * The logical groups the e2e specs are split into for CI.
 *
 * A group is derived from a spec's numeric prefix, so adding a spec never
 * requires editing this file or the workflow: the CI matrix is built from
 * `--list-groups`. An unrecognised decade still gets its own group, named
 * after the prefix, rather than being dropped from the run.
 *
 * Groups rather than `wdio --shard x/y` — which would balance better — so
 * that a failing check names what broke. Within-group imbalance is absorbed
 * by E2E_MAX_INSTANCES instead.
 */

import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import * as path from 'node:path';

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
export const SPEC_DIR = path.join(root, 'e2e', 'specs');

/** Prefix -> check name. A two-digit key wins over its decade, which is how a
 * single spec is lifted into a group of its own. */
const LABELS = {
  0: 'smoke',
  1: 'outline-mode',
  2: 'structural-commands',
  3: 'keyboard-grammar',
  4: 'shell',
  5: 'decorations',
  6: 'selection',
  7: 'backlinks',
  8: 'zoom',
  // Its own group: the longest spec in the suite, and its own feature.
  55: 'position-indicators',
  // Lifted out of `selection` and run one-at-a-time: see EXCLUSIVE_GROUPS.
  61: 'clipboard',
  62: 'clipboard',
  67: 'clipboard',
};

/**
 * Groups whose specs contend for a resource the MACHINE owns, and so cannot run
 * beside each other however many instances the runner is given.
 *
 * `clipboard` is the only one. `pasteText` writes the system clipboard and then
 * presses Mod+V, and 61 and 67 press Mod+C into that same system clipboard —
 * one clipboard per machine, three specs, and workers interleaving freely.
 * Observed twice on CI, in both directions: a paste receiving another spec's
 * copied fixture, and a copy losing its content before the spec could read it.
 *
 * Serialising them is the fix that keeps the tests honest. The tempting
 * alternative — synthesising a `paste` ClipboardEvent so no OS clipboard is
 * involved — would stop exercising a real paste, and the copy side cannot be
 * faked that way at all.
 *
 * Only these three are serialised, so the rest of `selection` keeps its
 * parallelism, and the new group is a CI job of its own (the matrix is built
 * from `--list-groups`) which runs alongside the others anyway.
 */
export const EXCLUSIVE_GROUPS = new Set(['clipboard']);

content.text:
Pushed as `c931299`.

**What failed:** `mobile (selection)` → `60-transaction-classification` → the ~2000-line stress note's p95 was **10ms against a budget of 8**. The median assertion passed.

**What I found before changing anything:**

- Every prior run on this branch passed, including `0b69a09` with all the earlier code changes. The failure appeared on `8d2993a` — the status-bar/toast commit.
- Locally the same test measures a **0.2ms maximum**, nowhere near 8. So the 10ms sample is contention on a runner sharing four Obsidian instances, not a slowdown in the code classification runs — nothing in that commit touches the filter's path.
- But the commit *did* change when the measurement window opens. `outlineNote` resets the stats the moment the mode flips, and reaching outline mode used to mean waiting on a 1.5s toast — several hundred milliseconds of incidental settling before the first measured keystroke. With the toast gone and the wait now a state poll, the window opens closer to the note's own warm-up, so a first-touch sample can land in it. With only ~70 samples, p95 is roughly the 4th-worst, so one outlier decides it.

**What I did:** stated the settle instead of inheriting it — a few driven edits, *then* the stats reset, then the measured run. **I did not touch the budget.** It's a per-keystroke contract from the enforcement design (D7), and moving it to make a red check go green would have quietly weakened a real guarantee to cover a test-timing artifact I introduced.

Verified: the spec passes on both desktop and mobile locally (9 each). Whether the contention outlier recurs is CI's to say — the re-run of `8d2993a` was still in progress when I checked, so if that one comes back green it confirms the flake reading, and this change makes the window less likely to catch one either way.

All six addressed, pushed as `479abbb`, threads replied to and resolved.

**Two were real coverage gaps, and both were my omissions:**

content.text:
Pushed as `88624a0`. No replies to post — this round was a review summary with two suppressed comments and no inline threads, so there was nothing carrying a `comment_id`.

**Both findings were real, and the first had siblings.** `Range` and `TreeWalker` are created *by* a document and scoped to it, so in a pop-out window the measurement was built against a document that doesn't contain the node it measures. Copilot named `createRange`; the two `createTreeWalker` calls feeding it have the identical defect, and fixing one of three would have left the path half-correct — all three now go through the view's `ownerDocument`, matching the realm check `zoom-click.ts` already makes for `Element` and the one I added for the frame clock. The `expect` import was mine: it went unused when `setOutlineMode` moved from asserting the state to waiting for it.

**One thing I deliberately did not change:** `svgEl`'s `document.createElementNS`. An element created in one document and appended into another is auto-adopted, which is *not* true of `Range`/`TreeWalker`, and it's a free function with no view in scope — threading a document to every call site would be churn for no defect.

Verified: `57-marker-gap` (5) and `56-list-grid` (30) both pass — those are the specs that consume `--to-space-advance`, so they're the ones that would break if I'd scoped the measurement wrong. Lint and both typechecks clean.

**Two observations worth your call, neither actioned:**

- **`e2e/` isn't linted.** That's why the unused import survived — `npm run lint` covers `src` and `tests` only. Extending it isn't cheap: `npx eslint e2e` reports 2114 problems, nearly all Obsidian plugin-guideline rules (`no-console` and friends) that are meaningless for test code. It'd need its own config block, so it's a separate change if you want it.
- **`decorations.ts:1646` registers `keydown` on the global `document`**, which in a pop-out window listens to the wrong one — the block-selection Escape handler wouldn't fire there. Pre-existing and outside anything this PR touched, so I left it; happy to spin it off as its own task.

content.text:
Pushed as `2fa1a98`.

**The failure was not a regression, and I checked rather than assumed.** `mobile (backlinks)` → `77-footer-controls` → `readStable` threw *"the footer never held one shape long enough to read"* — a poll waiting for the footer's layout to hold still. Three things say it's contention:

- The helper's **own comment already records** timing out on CI twice before ("measured reliably fast locally and still timed out on CI twice in a row, so 8 seconds is not everyone's floor").
- The spec **passes locally on both platforms** (23 each).
- **No slowdown from my work:** `mobile (backlinks)` ran 208s at `7c7bac6` — before any of the rAF/observer changes — and 184s at `c931299` after them. The 235s on the failing run includes the timeout it was burning.

Desktop backlinks passed on the same run, which also points at the mobile runner rather than the code.

**But the look did turn up one thing that was genuinely mine.** The post-layout pass I added was re-running the *entire* `apply()` — margins, facts, per-line chevron rows, the widget sweep — to recover two CSS custom properties. It exists for exactly one reason: two rect-reading measurements need a laid-out DOM and the constructor has none. Everything else in `apply()` is already driven by `docViewUpdate`. So it was doing far more than its reason called for, on every editor construction, on the note-open path where cost scales with note size. It now runs those two measurements and nothing else.

I was careful not to sell that as the fix. Disabling the deferred call fails `57-marker-gap`'s space-advance case, so it's still load-bearing; `56-list-grid` (30) and `57-marker-gap` (5) both pass, lint and typecheck clean.

If `mobile (backlinks)` fails again on this commit, that changes the picture — it would mean the contention reading is wrong and I'd look at `readStable`'s deadline or the group's parallelism rather than reaching for another code change.

Still held for your go: `openspec archive per-tab-outline-mode` and `npm version minor`.

TITLE: fix(e2e): retry an intercepted click alongside a stale one

## Why

CI run [34252974667](https://github.com/laughedelic/obsidian-true-outliner/actions/runs/34252974667), job `mobile (backlinks)`, failed
`75-footer-behaviour.e2e.ts > backlinks footer: behaviour > leaves the note's bytes and undo
stack untouched while being read` with

> `element click intercepted: Element <svg ... class="to-backlinks-icon"> is not clickable at point (195, 412). Other element would receive the click: <div class="nav-files-container node-insert-event">`

— the phone-viewport file-explorer drawer over the footer icon at click time. A plain re-run
went green and the tree had already passed the full matrix twice, which reads like timing.

**It is not timing.** The failure reproduced locally under mobile emulation and survived the
retry this PR originally proposed. Probing the workspace at the refused click:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `app.workspace.leftSplit.collapsed` | `false` |
| `.workspace-drawer.mod-left` rect | (0, 0) 327.6 x 844 |
| viewport | 390 x 844 |

The phone UI's file explorer is a drawer, and open it covers 327 of the 390 available pixels
— including the centre of the editor, exactly where `clickClear` scrolls its target. It read
open at both attempts ~15 s apart and closed on its own later in the session, which is why a
CI re-run goes green. No bounded wait inside one test closes it.

So `clickClear` collapses it on mobile runs. Nothing in the suite asserts the drawer's state.

## What the measurement changed

Two figures, both in the new [`docs/research/29-e2e-click-retry-costs.md`](docs/research/29-e2e-click-retry-costs.md).

**WebdriverIO already retries an intercepted click.** `elementClick` re-scrolls the element
to centre and re-issues the click — immediately — then lets the second failure through. So
the CI failure is not a click that was never retried; it is one retried without waiting,
against an obstruction that only time removes. `clickClear`'s pause is the layer that waits.

**An intercepted attempt is not cheap.** This change was drafted keeping the existing
four-attempt bound for both modes. Driving `clickClear` at a target covered for the whole

Pushed as `8b05645`. **I was wrong twice, and the correction matters.**

I called the previous two failures contention. They weren't. The `mobile (backlinks)` failure on `2fa1a98` is `75-footer-behaviour` failing with **`element click intercepted`** — the phone-viewport file-explorer drawer sitting over the footer icon at click time.

**This is already diagnosed, and the fix is one layer up in your own stack.** PR #81 (`fix/retry-intercepted-e2e-clicks`, stacked directly on #75) documents this exact failure — same spec, same element, same coordinates `(195, 412)` — and its body says plainly: *"It is not timing."* It measured the drawer at 327 of 390px, open at both click attempts ~15s apart, closing on its own only later. That's why re-runs go green and why I misread it.

**It isn't mine, and I checked rather than assumed:** #81's diagnosed occurrence was on `fix/heading-content-start-backspace` at 16:45, half an hour *before* my `leftSplit.expand()` landed at 17:10 — and the backlinks group is a separate CI job from the one my helper runs in, so it couldn't reach it anyway.

**What I did fix is a hazard I planted.** `clickIndicator` opened the left split to reach the ribbon and never closed it — the same drawer, left open for every later test in that session. It now restores the split to whatever it found (probed on mobile: collapsed before, collapsed after). Hygiene in my own code, not a fix for the check.

**What I deliberately did not do: port #81's `clickClear` fix down into #75.** It owns that change with its own OpenSpec change and research doc, and copying it here would conflict when #81 restacks — which is exactly the stack hazard you warned me about.

So the practical situation is yours to decide: **#75's red check is #81's bug, and #81 sits on top of #75.** Either merge #75 with that check known-red and let #81 land the fix immediately after, or reorder so the fix goes first. I'd take the first — the flake is intermittent, diagnosed, and owned.

Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

`<capability-path>` is the spec directory relative to `specs/` (for example, `user-auth` or `identity/user-auth`). Preserve the full path from each delta spec when resolving its main spec.

**Input**: Optionally specify a change name. If omitted, check if it can be inferred from conversation context. If vague or ambiguous you MUST prompt for available changes.

**Steps**

1. **Select the change**

   If a name is provided, use it. Otherwise:
   - Infer from conversation context if the user mentioned a change
   - Auto-select if only one active change exists
   - If ambiguous, run `openspec list --json` to get available changes and ask the user to select one

   When prompting, show only active changes (not already archived).
   Include the schema used for each change if available.

   Always announce: "Using change: <name>" and how to override (e.g., `/openspec-archive-change <other>`).

   **Load current archive inputs before the existing archive checks:**

   After resolving the selected change and planning root, run:
   ```bash
   openspec instructions archive --change "<name>" --json
   ```
   Keep the same selected-root flags on this command. This lookup is advisory and
   optional: it only supplies extra prompt inputs, so it must never block archiving.
   If it exits non-zero or returns invalid JSON — for example on an older CLI that
   does not support this command yet — continue the archive workflow with no
   context and no operation guidance. Do not report an error and do not stop.

   A successful response may omit both optional fields. Treat `context` as a
   required prompt-level input: read and consider it, and apply relevant project
   facts, conventions, and constraints. Treat `operationGuidance` as optional
   additive advice: read and consider every entry, and follow entries that are
   applicable and compatible with the built-in archive workflow.

   Keep both fields separate from built-in steps, explicit user choices, resolved
   paths, CLI checks, and command contracts. If context conflicts with one of those
   controlling inputs, report the conflict and preserve the controlling value. If
   guidance is inapplicable or conflicts with a controlling input, do not follow it
   and explain why. Do not infer replacement paths, skipped prompts, or flags from
   either field, and do not copy their text verbatim into specs, change artifacts,
   or archive summaries unless the user separately asks for it. These are
   prompt-level behavior contracts, not enforceable checks.

2. **Check artifact completion status**

   Run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json` to check artifact completion.

   Parse the JSON to understand:
   - `schemaName`: The workflow being used
   - `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, `artifactPaths`, and `actionContext`: path and scope context
   - `artifacts`: List of artifacts with their status (`done`, `skipped`, or other)

   **If any artifacts are neither `done` nor `skipped`** (skipped artifacts satisfy the requirement - the change declares skip_specs):
   - Display warning listing incomplete artifacts
   - Ask the user to confirm they want to proceed
   - Proceed if user confirms

3. **Check task completion status**

   Read the tasks file (typically `tasks.md`) to check for incomplete tasks.

   Count tasks marked with `- [ ]` (incomplete) vs `- [x]` (complete).

   **If incomplete tasks found:**
   - Display warning showing count of incomplete tasks
   - Ask the user to confirm they want to proceed
   - Proceed if user confirms

   **If no tasks file exists:** Proceed without task-related warning.

4. **Assess delta spec sync state**

   Use `artifactPaths.specs.existingOutputPaths` from status JSON as the only
   delta-spec source. If the `specs` entry is missing or
   `existingOutputPaths` is empty, proceed without a sync prompt and do not infer
   delta specs from other artifacts.

   **If delta specs exist:**
   - Compare each delta spec with its corresponding main spec at `<planningHome.root>/openspec/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md` (use the store-aware `planningHome.root` from step 2, not a hardcoded repo path)
   - Determine what changes would be applied (adds, modifications, removals, renames)
   - Show a combined summary before prompting

   **Prompt options:**
   - If changes needed: "Sync now (recommended)", "Archive without syncing"
   - If already synced: "Archive now", "Sync anyway", "Cancel"

   Route on the answer:
   - "Cancel" — stop, do not archive
   - "Archive without syncing" or "Archive now" — proceed to archive
   - "Sync now" or "Sync anyway" — sync, then verify (below)
   - Anything else — ask again rather than archiving

   Before a selected sync writes any main spec, run
   `openspec instructions specs --change "<name>" --json` once with the same
   selected-root flags. Require a zero exit status and valid artifact-instruction
   JSON. If the lookup fails or returns invalid JSON, report the error and stop
   before writing any main spec or moving the change. A valid response with omitted
   `rules` is the no-rules case. Apply returned `rules` only to the content and
   form of main specs produced by this merge; do not use them as archive guidance,
   change CLI behavior, or copy the rule text into any output file.

   Then run the `openspec-sync-specs` workflow inline (agent-driven intelligent merge) for change '<name>', passing the delta spec analysis and the fetched specs-rule snapshot from above, and wait for it to finish. The inline sync must reuse that snapshot without fetching `specs` instructions again. Do not delegate it to a background task — step 5 would move `changeRoot` out from under a sync that is still reading it, leaving the change archived and the main specs never updated. If your agent can only run it by delegation, delegate synchronously and wait for the result.

   Then re-run the comparison from the top of this step against every capability that has a delta spec in `artifactPaths.specs.existingOutputPaths` — not only the ones the sync reports it touched. A successful sync leaves nothing left to apply, so each capability must now read as already synced:
   - ADDED requirements present
   - MODIFIED requirements carrying the scenario and description changes named in the delta, with their other scenarios intact
   - REMOVED requirements gone — and where this sync retired a capability (removed its last requirement, leaving `## Requirements` empty), its main spec deleted rather than left empty; a spec the sync deliberately kept and reported is also a match
   - RENAMED requirements present under the new name and absent under the old one

   If the sync failed, or any capability does not match, report what differs and stop — do not archive. Nothing has moved and `changeRoot` is intact, so the user can fix the mismatch or re-run the sync and start the archive again.

5. **Perform the archive**

   Create an `archive` directory under `planningHome.changesDir` if it doesn't exist:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p "<planningHome.changesDir>/archive"
   ```

   Generate the target name: use the change name as-is when it already starts with a `YYYY-MM-DD-` prefix; otherwise prepend the current date as `YYYY-MM-DD-<change-name>`. Never stack a second date (same rule as `openspec archive`).

   **Check if target already exists:**
   - If yes: Fail with error, suggest renaming existing archive or using different date
   - If no: Move `changeRoot` to the archive directory

   ```bash
   mv "<changeRoot>" "<planningHome.changesDir>/archive/<target-name>"
   ```

6. **Display summary**

   Show archive completion summary including:
   - Change name
   - Schema that was used
   - Archive location
   - Whether specs were synced (if applicable)
   - Note about any warnings (incomplete artifacts/tasks)

```markdown

**Change:** <change-name>
**Schema:** <schema-name>
**Archived to:** the archive path derived from `planningHome.changesDir`/<target-name>/
**Specs:** <"✓ Synced to main specs" only if the step 4 verification passed; otherwise "No delta specs" or "Sync skipped">

<"All artifacts complete. All tasks complete." — or, if archived with warnings, list them instead (e.g. "Archived with 2 incomplete tasks")>
```

**Guardrails**
- Announce the selected change; prompt for selection when it is ambiguous
- Use artifact graph (openspec status --json) for completion checking
- Don't block archive on warnings - just inform and confirm
- Preserve .openspec.yaml when moving to archive (it moves with the directory)

- Artifact rules constrain only the specs being written and are never operation guidance
- Never copy runtime context, operation guidance, or artifact-rule text verbatim into output files
